key_concept: Photorespiration occurs when RuBisCO acts as an oxygenase: it binds $O_2$ instead of $CO_2$, giving phosphoglycolate, and the pathway releases $CO_2$ without making ATP or NADPH.
steps: Statement (a): Photorespiration is typical of $C_3$ plants. In $C_4$ plants it is minimised because $CO_2$ is concentrated around RuBisCO in the bundle sheath. So (a) is incorrect.

Statement (b): In photorespiration, $O_2$ is consumed (RuBisCO oxygenase activity) and $CO_2$ is released (in mitochondria, when glycine is converted to serine). The statement reverses this, so (b) is incorrect.
Statement (c): RuBisCO adds $O_2$ to RuBP ($5C$), giving one molecule of 3-phosphoglycerate ($3C$) and one of 2-phosphoglycolate ($2C$). So (c) is correct.
Statement (d): Photorespiration is a wasteful process. There is no synthesis of ATP or NADPH; instead ATP is used up. So (d) is correct.
The correct statements are (c) and (d), which matches option (2).
why_not_others: Options (1) and (4) include (a), but photorespiration is characteristic of $C_3$ plants. Options (3) and (4) include (b), which reverses the gas exchange: $O_2$ is consumed and $CO_2$ is released.
common_trap: Students confuse photorespiration with photosynthesis and mark (b), forgetting that photorespiration takes up $O_2$ and gives out $CO_2$.
time_saving_tip: Rejecting (a) alone eliminates options (1) and (4). Then (b) is clearly reversed, which leaves only option (2).
